newsitem.title: USA: Clinton seems unruffled by U.S. stock market rise.
newsitem.headline: Clinton seems unruffled by U.S. stock market rise.

text.p: President Bill Clinton said on Thursday the U.S. stock market has produced "remarkable growth," adding that the economy itself has performed well and enjoys prospects for further growth with low inflation.

"The market has produced a remarkable growth, but the economy is growing," Clinton said at a joint news conference with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. "Obviously, the concern is whether returns to stocks, returns to investement, are greater than can be justified based on the productivity and profit prospects of the companies that are being traded."

"But if you look at the stability and the growth that we have enjoyed and the prospects we have for stable growth with no inflation, it's hard to say that it's completely out of the question," he added. The Dow Jones industrial average rose 60.81 points to close at a record 7,022.44 on Thursday.

"Some people say: 'gosh we dont' want another 1987 here,' but even after 1987 we had a rather rapid rebound," Clinton said. "So I think what I need to do is try to work on keeping the economy healthy, let's go on and balance the budget, let's invest in our future ... let's follow our strategy and then let the market take care of itself -- as long as there's no destructive element in it. That's what I think we should do."
